problem: Models trained on safety objectives can be vulnerably compromised by adversarial attacks that transfer across architecturally different models, but the underlying mechanism of this transferability is unclear.
approach: Analyze representational similarity and jailbreak strength across 20 models and 33 attacks to identify systematic patterns; validate causality through benign-only distillation that increases transferability.
contribution: Demonstrates that jailbreak transferability emerges from shared representations rather than incidental safety training flaws; natural-language attacks exploit shared representation space while cipher-based attacks rely on model-specific quirks.

problem: Code language models represent valuable intellectual property but face threats of model theft and unauthorized redistribution; existing watermarking methods struggle with conflicting requirements of code generation.
approach: Leverage semantic-preserving transformations with dead-code augmentation and dual-LoRA shadow training plus optimizable trigger prompts for watermark extraction.
contribution: CodeGenGuard achieves superior watermarking performance for code LMs, robust to both benign transformations and adversarial removal attacks.

problem: Video-to-audio generation methods rely on text prompts that suffer from semantic granularity gaps and textual ambiguity in describing fine-grained acoustic features like different dog barks or microacoustic transients.
approach: Condition audio generation directly on reference audio signals rather than text descriptions, enabling precise acoustic attribute manipulation through timbre transfer.
contribution: AC-Foley achieves fine-grained Foley generation with state-of-the-art performance, enabling zero-shot generation of sounds and timbre transfer without training on specific datasets.

problem: Diffusion language models enable any-order generation but enlarge the attack surface; harmful content can appear at arbitrary positions and template-based prefilling attacks bypass response-level refusals.
approach: Align diffusion models at token-level to emit refusal signals when harmful content emerges, using randomized masking to achieve robustness across any decoding order and prefilling conditions.
contribution: A2D slashes DIJA attack success rates from over 80% to near-zero (0-1.3% depending on model) while enabling real-time monitoring and early rejection.

problem: Diffusion Transformers achieve high-quality image and video synthesis but suffer from computational bottlenecks due to iterative sampling requiring expensive transformer forward passes at each timestep.
approach: Model hidden feature evolution as mixture of ODEs across dimensions and apply dimension-wise caching strategies using hybrid ODE solvers instead of uniform caching.
contribution: HyCa achieves 5.56-6.24x speedup on models like FLUX and HunyuanVideo without retraining, with near-lossless acceleration across diverse domains.

problem: Large multimodal models struggle with physical world understanding due to lack of spatial representation and inability to capture temporally varying dynamic objects in scenes.
approach: Generate spatiotemporal prompts by encoding 3D positions and 1D time into dynamic-aware 4D coordinate embeddings, then align visual and language embeddings through these structured prompts.
contribution: LLaVA-4D enables 4D scene understanding distinguishing static backgrounds from dynamic objects; demonstrates superiority on various 4D reasoning tasks.

problem: Sparse autoencoders are widely used for interpretability but quality metrics and automatic explanation pipelines may not actually measure mechanistic interpretability.
approach: Test whether SAE metrics and interpretability scores can distinguish trained from randomly initialized transformers across multiple Pythia model sizes and randomization schemes.
contribution: Many SAE quality metrics and auto-interpretability scores produce similar results for trained and random models, showing these metrics alone do not guarantee learned, computationally relevant features.

problem: Vision-language alignment methods like CLIP maximize mutual information via pairwise alignment but overlook distributional differences between modalities, leading to suboptimal alignment with modality gaps.
approach: Integrate Cauchy-Schwarz divergence with mutual information to capture both global distribution information and pairwise semantic relationships in a unified framework.
contribution: CS-Aligner addresses the alignment-uniformity conflict inherent in InfoNCE, enabling tighter alignment and incorporation of unpaired data and token-level representations.

problem: Vision-language-action models remain underexplored for professional science domains like digital biology labs where precision manipulation and structured protocols are required.
approach: Develop simulation framework and benchmark with digitized laboratory instruments, specialized physics plugins, and physically-based rendering; provide infrastructure for demonstration generation and VLA model integration.
contribution: AutoBio benchmark reveals significant gaps in precision manipulation and visual reasoning of SOTA VLA models on laboratory workflows, establishing baseline for science-oriented robotic systems.

problem: Nearest neighbor search for retrieval-augmented applications like web search and recommendation systems must balance competing objectives of relevance and diversity across attributes.
approach: Apply welfare-based formulations from mathematical economics to NNS using Nash social welfare functions that adaptively balance relevance and diversity in query-dependent manner.
contribution: Develops efficient nearest neighbor algorithms with provable guarantees for welfare-based objectives that can layer on top of standard ANN methods.

problem: Large language models face threats of theft and misuse; existing fingerprinting methods struggle to provide verifiable ownership while resisting adversarial removal and fine-tuning.
approach: Develop cryptographic chain-and-hash fingerprinting that binds prompts to responses; incorporate random padding and varied meta-prompt configurations during training for robustness.
contribution: Framework securely proves model ownership, resists benign transformations and adversarial removal, and extends to fingerprinting LoRA adapters.

problem: Vision-language rerankers like BLIP are bottlenecked by expensive visual feature extraction, preventing practical deployment for large-scale multimodal retrieval at high throughput.
approach: Precompute vision tokens offline and compress via lightweight attention-based adapter, enabling online inference with only compact joint encoder over small visual token set.
contribution: EDJE processes 50k image-text pairs/second with 49kB disk storage per image while matching prior art on Flickr and COCO retrieval benchmarks.

problem: Deep neural networks are adversarially fragile compared to optimal classifiers; the fundamental source of this fragility is unclear.
approach: Provide matrix-theoretic explanation showing adversarial robustness degrades as input dimension increases; show neural network robustness can be only 1/sqrt(d) of optimal classifiers.
contribution: Theoretical analysis explains adversarial fragility through feature compression; predictions match experiments on practical networks including ImageNet models.

problem: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting methods struggle to balance high-frequency rendering details with high-frequency motion, causing motion blur in 4D novel view synthesis.
approach: Introduce frequency-differentiated Gaussian kernels for adaptive alpha-blending and Fourier-Deformation Network using high-frequency embeddings to capture diverse motion patterns.
contribution: FAGS significantly reduces motion blur and enhances structural details, achieving state-of-the-art 4D reconstruction performance on synthetic and real-world benchmarks.

problem: Few-shot text classification requires both efficiency and interpretability, but large language models are expensive and lack interpretability while concept bottleneck models need expensive surrogate model training.
approach: Develop concept bottleneck model paradigm relying solely on sample-concept similarity with prototypical-discriminative dual-level architecture and dynamic concept refinement.
contribution: With only 10 training samples, achieves performance comparable to LLMs while providing interpretable concept-based predictions.

problem: Multimodal large language models struggle to activate complex reasoning capabilities like questioning and reflection due to scarcity of high-quality multimodal reasoning data.
approach: Construct high-quality multimodal chain-of-thought dataset without human annotation via modality bridging; employ Progressive Thinking Suppression Training and Group Relative Policy Optimization.
contribution: Vision-R1-7B achieves 73.5% accuracy on MathVista benchmark, only 0.4% lower than OpenAI O1, with average 6% improvement across multimodal math reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Latent diffusion for time series suffers from posterior collapse, degenerating into weaker variational autoencoder models with exponentially decreasing latent variable impact over time.
approach: Introduce dependency measures quantifying decoder sensitivity to inputs; interpret diffusion as variational inference and eliminate risky KL regularization while penalizing decoder insensitivity.
contribution: Posterior-stable latent diffusion maintains stable posterior and outperforms previous baselines in time series synthesis.

problem: Independence testing for determining whether two variables are independent may sacrifice statistical power when applied to limited samples with background knowledge of distribution.
approach: For linear non-Gaussian data, characterize independence through constancy of conditional mean and variance; develop kernel-based testing framework with asymptotic guarantees.
contribution: Achieves higher statistical power than existing approaches and significantly improves downstream causal discovery performance.

problem: Learning-based high dynamic range fusion methods have limited generalization due to scarcity of large-scale training data; collecting HDR images from dynamic scenes is costly and technically challenging.
approach: Create first large-scale synthetic HDR dataset (24,000 samples) using Unreal Engine 5 with diverse realistic scenes; develop S2R-Adapter for domain adaptation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art HDR fusion performance on real-world datasets, bridging synthetic-to-real domain gap.

problem: Sparse Autoencoders have rarely been applied outside textual domain; feature decomposition in 3D models remains unexplored, limiting understanding of how features encode discrete vs continuous information.
approach: Apply SAEs to 3D reconstruction VAE analyzing 53k Objaverse models; model feature evolution through phase-like transitions across feature dimensions.
contribution: First SAE application to 3D domain reveals networks approximate discrete state space; explains unexpected phenomena including positional encoding preference and bimodal phase transitions.

problem: Existing AI-generated image detection methods are black boxes that fail on out-of-distribution data, while multimodal LLMs provide reasoning but often hallucinate without grounding.
approach: Construct FakeXplained dataset with bounding boxes and captions highlighting synthesis artifacts; fine-tune MLLMs with progressive training to enable artifact localization and textual explanations.
contribution: FakeXplainer achieves 98.2% detection accuracy and 36.0% IoU while providing spatially grounded, human-aligned rationales with strong out-of-distribution generalization.

problem: Monocular 3D reconstruction methods and vision-language models demonstrate impressive results on standard benchmarks, but their true understanding of geometric properties remains unclear.
approach: Develop comprehensive benchmark with synthetic and real-world images of diverse polyhedra; evaluate through 3D reconstruction, symmetry detection, mental rotation, and shape classification tasks.
contribution: Reveals significant shortcomings: SOTA algorithms struggle reconstructing basic geometric forms; VLMs falter on tasks requiring detailed geometric differentiation.

problem: Diffusion-based language models enable parallel token generation but suffer from static sampling strategies leading to suboptimal efficiency and limited flexibility.
approach: Propose SlowFast Sampling that adaptively alternates between exploratory and accelerated decoding stages guided by certainty, convergence, and positional principles; integrate with dLLM-Cache.
contribution: Achieves up to 15.63x speedup on LLaDA and 34.22x with caching; outperforms autoregressive baselines in throughput while maintaining minimal accuracy drop.

problem: Aligning large language models to simultaneously satisfy multiple objectives remains challenging given diverse and often conflicting human preferences.
approach: Introduce Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts combining LoRA Experts, Router Experts, and Weighting Router to enable adaptation across Pareto frontier without retraining.
contribution: HoE eliminates retraining while enabling LLMs to accommodate diverse preferences; demonstrates superior performance across 16 objectives and 200 preference configurations.

problem: Instruction-tuned vision-language models struggle with medical imaging due to medical attributes encoded as plain text collapsing semantically distinct concepts, causing inter-attribute confusion.
approach: Introduce attribute tokens uniquely encoding clinical attributes in structured token space with attribute-centric embedding books; design attribute-centric cross-attention adapter and matching loss.
contribution: AttTok substantially improves discriminative accuracy on five medical classification benchmarks and three VQA datasets through structured attribute alignment.

problem: Conformal prediction provides coverage guarantees but efficiency depends on prediction set size; prior work treats miscoverage level as fixed constant without analyzing sample complexity.
approach: Establish non-asymptotic bounds on deviation of prediction set length from oracle interval for conformalized quantile and median regression trained via SGD.
contribution: Bounds of order O(1/sqrt(n) + 1/(alpha^2*n) + 1/sqrt(m) + exp(-alpha^2*m)) reveal phase transitions in convergence rates across regimes.

problem: Offline model-based reinforcement learning must handle uncertainty about true MDP since multiple MDPs can behave identically on static datasets.
approach: Model offline MBRL as Bayes Adaptive MDP and propose Bayes Adaptive Monte-Carlo planning algorithm based on MCTS for continuous state-action spaces.
contribution: RL plus search framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art offline RL methods on D4RL MuJoCo tasks and stochastic tokamak control.

problem: Single-image 3D face reconstruction requires inferring complex 3D geometry from limited 2D input while handling diverse expressions, viewing angles, and ethnicities.
approach: Develop generalized vision transformers predicting per-pixel geometric cues to constrain morphable face model optimization; use DINO latent features with surface normal and UV-coordinate heads.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art by over 15% in geometric accuracy; first benchmark evaluating both posed and neutral facial geometry across diverse demographics.

problem: Unsupervised pre-training for reinforcement learning must generate effective goals across diverse downstream tasks where solving every task zero-shot is infeasible.
approach: Optimize for efficient multi-episode exploration and adaptation within meta-learning framework; guide curriculum with evolving post-adaptation performance estimates.
contribution: ULEE pre-training yields improved exploration and adaptation that generalizes to novel objectives, environment dynamics, and map structures.

problem: Molecule-protein interaction prediction faces scarcity of labeled pairs and ignores broader biological context like genes and metabolic pathways.
approach: Aggregate diverse biological datasets and develop optimal-transport approach to generate high-quality pseudo-labels for unlabeled molecule-protein pairs.
contribution: Substantial improvements over state-of-the-art in prediction accuracy and zero-shot ability; demonstrates new paradigm for leveraging heterogeneous biological data.

problem: Search-augmented LLMs suffer from unreliability in multi-hop reasoning due to decomposition errors, retrieval misses, and reasoning errors that propagate through chains.
approach: Identify faulty reasoning steps, erase them, and regenerate reasoning in place through erasable reinforcement learning framework.
contribution: ESearch achieves +8.48% EM and +11.56% F1 on HotpotQA for 3B model and +5.38% EM and +7.22% F1 for 7B model over prior SOTA.

problem: Vision-language models like CLIP remain highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations despite strong zero-shot generalization.
approach: Uncover dominant direction in adversarial feature space shifts; estimate Defense Direction and employ two-stream reconstruction strategy to recover robust representations.
contribution: DBD achieves state-of-the-art adversarial robustness while preserving clean accuracy; shows adversarial accuracy can surpass clean accuracy.

problem: Flow-matching policies enable multi-modal action distributions but suffer from prohibitive inference latency and ineffective online exploration.
approach: Introduce Q-guided prior modeled by conditional VAE for one-step distillation; enable stochastic distribution output with entropy regularization for principled exploration.
contribution: GoldenStart achieves efficient and exploratory policies by designing generative startpoint and controlling entropy; bridges generative models and practical RL.

problem: Language models generate tokens sequentially without deliberative cognitive effort, limiting ability to tackle complex problems requiring deeper processing.
approach: Enable pondering by repeatedly invoking forward process within single token generation step; model ponders by yielding weighted sum of embeddings then feeds back as input.
contribution: PonderPythia-2.8B surpasses Pythia-6.9B and rivals Pythia-12B; PonderPythia-1B matches TinyLlama-1.1B trained on 10 times more data.

problem: Large language models struggle with multi-step reasoning due to gap between sparse-reward RL and rigid token-mimicry supervised fine-tuning.
approach: Reformulate problem-solving as sequence of logical actions; train model to generate internal reasoning monologue then commit to action with dense step-wise rewards.
contribution: Supervised Reinforcement Learning significantly outperforms both RLVR and SFT; curriculum combining SRL cold-start with RLVR refinement achieves strongest results.

problem: Scaling Transformers to ultra-long contexts is bottlenecked by O(n^2*d) cost of self-attention; existing sequence-axis approaches consistently degrade accuracy.
approach: Explore orthogonal feature-sparsity axis where queries and keys are k-sparse codes; introduce FlashSFA IO-aware kernel for efficient sparse overlap computation.
contribution: Sparse Feature Attention matches dense baselines while improving speed 2.5x and reducing FLOPs and KV-cache by 50%; preserves retrieval accuracy at long contexts.

problem: Autoregressive video diffusion models lack fine-grained control to ensure outputs consistently align with user expectations.
approach: Enable streaming drag-oriented interactive video manipulation anytime on anything; employ adaptive distribution self-rectification and spatial-frequency selective optimization.
contribution: DragStream achieves streaming drag on diffusion videos while mitigating latent distribution drift and context frame interference.

problem: Cognitive load prediction in real-world settings is fundamentally constrained by poor and variable quality of physiological signals, limiting deployment outside labs.
approach: Propose signal-quality-guided Mixture-of-Experts framework that dynamically adapts to heterogeneous inputs through quality-aware gating and two-stage processing pipeline.
contribution: CogMoE outperforms baselines with consistent improvements across diverse signal qualities; introduces CORTEX Loss balancing reconstruction and expert utilization.

problem: Conformal prediction for time series faces challenges adapting to feature and non-conformity score correlations and constructing prediction sets for multi-dimensional outcomes.
approach: Use flow with classifier-free guidance for conformal prediction; provide coverage guarantees through exact marginal coverage and finite-sample conditional coverage bounds.
contribution: Constructs significantly smaller prediction sets than existing methods while maintaining target coverage on real-world time series datasets.

problem: Vision-language-action models either rely on external experts for modality unification or treat image generation and action prediction as separate processes.
approach: Couple understanding, generation, and action through synchronous denoising diffusion where action tokens progressively attend to future image tokens via hybrid attention.
contribution: Unified Diffusion VLA achieves state-of-the-art on CALVIN, LIBERO, and SimplerEnv; demonstrates effectiveness through real-world evaluations.
